items.Sentence: Influent raw sewage flow that exceeds the operational setpoint is diverted to equalization ponds (Ponds 1A and 1B) by a control valve.
The headworks consist of two micro screens, a Parshall flume, a grit chamber, and weirs for flow control and distribution.
The headworks consist of two micro screens, a Parshall flume, a grit chamber, and weirs for flow control and distribution.
Screened influent flows from the grit chamber to one of two 95-foot diameter conventional primary clarifiers with a design capacity of 15 MGD each.
The CEPT uses a coagulant (ferric chloride and an anionic emulsion polymer) to enhance flocculation and coagulation during primary clarification.

Each basin has been configured as the Modified Ludzack Ettinger (MLE) activated sludge process. The MLE process consists of an anoxic zone followed by an aerobic zone, with internal mixed liquor recycle...for denitrification of ammonia oxidized to nitrate in the aerobic zone.
The secondary treatment system consists of three aeration basins and four secondary clarifiers.

Scum and Waste Activated Sludge (WAS) are pumped to the DAFT mixing facility prior to conveyance to the primary anaerobic digesters. The Facility also has two DAFT units which may be utilized to thicken primary solids and WAS.

secondary effluent...is directed to either a cloth-media disk filter system or a conventional deep-bed, dual media filter system. Currently all flow is being filtered using the cloth media filtration system, with the conventional media filters held in standby.
Chlorine gas is stored in 1-ton containers and is used to make a concentrated chlorine/water solution to disinfect the filtered secondary effluent.
A sulfur dioxide/water solution is injected into the secondary effluent flow stream for dechlorination near the outfall building.

Biodegradation of organic materials and production of methane gas and carbon dioxide take place in the primary digesters, which are continually mixed and heated within the mesophilic temperature range (approximately 95°F).

Historically, Ponds 3A, 3B, 5A, and 5B were used as the Facility's facultative sludge lagoons (FSLs); however upgrades to the Facility's solids treatment and handling processes has negated the need of the FSLs for solids stabilization.
Centrate from the dewatering process is currently routed to Pond 5A and 5B for equalization and ultimately metered back to the Facility headworks for treatment.
After digestion sludge is dewatered by one of the Facility's two centrifuges.
Dried biosolids are hauled to a landfill.
Biosolids will be dried to approximately 80 percent solids. The dried solids will enter the pyrolysis unit and be heated to 1400 degrees Fahrenheit.
